Reviewed the mode metadata showing parallel execution, three subagents, timeout, completed evaluation, and 0 of 40 official tests passed.
Reviewed the official status, including swarm-mode protocol evidence, artifact file list, timeout, and completed evaluator result of 0/40.
Reviewed the evaluator summary confirming the official Docker evaluation completed successfully and the submitted parallel solution passed 0 of 40 tests.

timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed the server event stream showing session creation, parent oracle probes, file writes, child swarm launch, offset-child interruption, cancelled turn, and final idle state.
Reviewed the session index mapping the parallel Kimi session to the mounted workspace and session directory.
Reviewed the clip child timeline: it implemented `clip.rs`, ran a focused harness, verified triangle intersection area 5000, and reported the full program still panicked at the offset stub.

Reviewed the offset child timeline: it read the stub and geometry, repeatedly probed and reverse-engineered Clipper2 offset behavior, wrote only scratch harnesses, and was cancelled without a final offset implementation.
Reviewed the formatting child timeline: it implemented `fmt.rs`, built exact-format harnesses, compared against glibc and C++ oracle outputs, and returned a completed handoff.

Reviewed the parent timeline: it performed serial pre-probing, created root skeleton files, launched three fixed-file children, received two completed and one aborted subagent result, and was cancelled.

timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed the serial server event stream showing one main actor probing the oracle, writing implementation files, compiling, comparing, continuing investigation, and then timing out.
Reviewed the session index mapping the serial Kimi session to the mounted workspace and session directory.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the fixed Clipper2 workload, exact CLI/output requirements, pure-std Rust constraint, and need to place `test7.rs` plus supporting modules in `/output`.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It created a root Cargo skeleton and split ownership into three children: `clip.rs`, `offset.rs`, and `fmt.rs`, with the parent implicitly responsible for assembling whatever returned.
parallel.implementation: The clip and formatter children completed their scoped files and local checks; the critical offset child only produced scratch probes and never delivered a replacement for the stub offset module.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received a swarm result with two completed children and one aborted offset child at cancellation time; no follow-up integration or takeover occurred after that result.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification was component-level for clip and formatting, with a visible full-program panic at the offset stub and no completed integrated oracle sweep.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The required `InflatePaths` implementation was unfinished, the run timed out, and the official evaluator completed with 0 of 40 tests passed.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same fixed workload, no-crates constraint, default offset argument, exact C++ formatting, and the need to produce a complete `/output` Cargo project.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, formatting, offset modeling, compilation, and final verification without child handoffs or separate module owners.
serial.implementation: It wrote `Cargo.toml`, `test7.rs`, and `src` modules including a substantive but approximate offset algorithm, then iterated on probes and debugger extraction.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It delivered an integrated project including a compiled `test7` binary and source files under `src`, with no cross-agent merge step required.
serial.verification: It compiled the project, compared many offsets to the reference binary, saw systematic mismatches, and continued reverse engineering until timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The offset implementation remained inaccurate, the actor was cancelled while investigating, and the official evaluator passed only 5 of 40 tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run saw the required Rust port, exact numeric behavior, no external crates, and root `test7.rs` deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run saw the same requirements and probed the reference executable for offsets and default argument behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar; the later difference came from how the required offset behavior was pursued and delivered.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed into three children and gave one child the entire critical `offset.rs` module.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had no subagents and one actor owned all implementation stages.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel isolated the hardest task in one child while serial kept offset modeling integrated with the rest of the workflow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child briefs specified module paths, fixed signatures, shared `geom.rs`, no-crate rules, and oracle expectations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single actor had the full task context continuously available while writing all modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no strong evidence of missing interface context; the failing boundary was the size and lifecycle of the offset assignment.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote the skeleton, completed clip and formatting modules, but left offset in the stub path because the offset child never delivered an implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a complete set of project files including `src/offset.rs`, `src/clip.rs`, `src/fmt.rs`, and `test7.rs`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had an integrated but imperfect offset algorithm; parallel effectively lacked the required offset implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received an `AgentSwarm` result showing two completed children and the required offset child aborted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; the single actor kept its partial implementation in the workspace while continuing to debug.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel depended on a child result that never arrived; serial's partial work was already present in the final workspace.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a shared `/output` workspace with fixed per-file ownership and side-effect writes from children; no same-file collision was visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself under one project layout and did not require a merge across actors.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The shared-state risk did not materialize as a collision; the delivery difference was the missing offset module in parallel versus serial's integrated source tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had local child checks for clip and formatting, but the full program still reached the offset stub and no integrated oracle sweep completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial compiled and ran broad oracle comparisons, saw mismatches, and continued debugging rather than declaring success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's tests exercised the integrated binary; parallel verification stopped at completed sibling modules because the critical offset stage never returned.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent its remaining budget waiting on the offset child; the child and parent were cancelled before a final answer or takeover.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but only after producing a compiled partial implementation and continuing the reverse-engineering loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed by timeout, but parallel closure stranded the indispensable child output whereas serial closure preserved a working partial project.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is `both_fail`: parallel failed 0/40 and serial failed 5/40. The score gap is nevertheless concrete. Parallel left the critical offset stage unfinished because that whole hard module was assigned to one child that was cancelled before handoff; clip and formatting work were not enough to produce correct end-to-end behavior. Serial also timed out and kept an inaccurate offset model, but it had written and compiled an integrated offset implementation before cancellation, enough for partial testcase coverage.
parallel_contributors: The offset module was delegated as a single broad critical child task and did not return a final implementation before cancellation.
The parent received the swarm result at cancellation time and did not complete a takeover or integrated verification pass.
serial_contributors: The serial actor wrote an integrated offset implementation and executable before timeout.
The serial actor used reference-output comparisons to find mismatches, but its model still remained incomplete.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts struggled with exact Clipper2 round offset behavior; serial's partial algorithm was an ordinary approximation defect, while parallel lacked the module due to the child lifecycle.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors to quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a pass/fail discordance

candidates.reason: The parent assigned implementation ownership for each required module, including the critical offset file, so implementation was not ownerless.
The component interfaces were fixed by the parent skeleton and there is no evidence that independent completed components were left incompatible for lack of an integration owner.
The parent created the root Cargo skeleton and entry file, so final assembly had an owner; the missing deliverable stage was the unfinished offset implementation.
The parent retained orchestration of the overall pipeline through the swarm call; the failure was not an unowned end-to-end transition but an unfinished critical child.

The parent did some serial probing before delegation, but implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory oracle gate as the retained episode; the concrete unfinished work was the overbroad offset child.

Investigation did not complete as a separate phase before all implementation; the parent launched implementation children after an initial probe, and the offset child worked directly on implementation probes.
The critical offset path had a worker, but that one assignment was itself overbroad; starvation is the less specific description of the same chain.
The parallel run used only three children and there is no evidence that excessive breadth or retries collectively exhausted the budget.

The parent assigned the entire Clipper2 `InflatePaths` reverse-engineering problem to one child, including exact all-probe matching, integer rounding, and cleanup behavior, and that child was cancelled without delivering the required implementation.
candidates.realized_consequence: The indispensable offset implementation was not completed or handed off in parallel; the submitted run passed 0/40 while the serial integrated attempt passed 5/40.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child was cancelled, but the cancellation is the terminal symptom of the overbroad one-child offset assignment rather than an independent timing error.

The completed clip and formatting reports were usable, and the offset child did not return an overlarge completed handoff for the parent to reduce.

The completed child reports did not contain incompatible contracts requiring adjudication; no conflicting handoffs blocked integration.
The parallel parent did not make an observable whole-task completion claim after receiving the aborted swarm result; the turn was cancelled.
No replacement or retry child was launched after the offset child stalled, so there was no checkpoint-free repeated-work episode.

retained_patterns.reason: A single child was asked to solve the full critical Clipper2 round-offset implementation, including exact oracle fitting and cleanup. The child stayed in reverse-engineering probes until cancellation and produced no usable offset module, while serial at least wrote an integrated offset implementation.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The required offset implementation was not completed or handed off in the parallel run, causing a fully failed official submission at 0/40 and lower coverage than serial's partial integrated attempt.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The child was interrupted, but the more specific corrective boundary is the overbroad one-child allocation of the critical offset module.
